messages:
maria: Heads-up — Customer Alpha signed a 12-month Dedicated commit for 48 A100-equivalent GPUs in us-west-2. Can we do a quick sizing sanity-check? They want predictable throughput for chat & embeddings, and a canary rollout plan. cc @jon @kevin

jon: Congrats. Quick Qs: what's their peak qps and model mix? chat (llama-2-ish) vs embeddings (sparse, high-batch)?

maria: Their SRE sent usage profile: 95th percentile concurrent chat sessions ~1,800, avg prompt+response ~700 tokens. Embeddings jobs are batched overnight, ~200 reqs/min with 512-dim vectors. Models: 80% chat on a fp16 30B, 20% embeddings on a smaller encoder. They'd like 99th p90 latency SLA for chat.

kevin: Back-of-envelope: our p95 tokens/sec per A100-equivalent with current kernel set ~30k tokens/s under production mix. For 1,800 concurrent sessions * 700 tokens each if they all run simultaneously that's worst-case burst = 1,260,000 tokens. But sessions are staggered. If expected steady-state is ~15k tokens/s, 48 GPUs gives 1.44M tokens/s capacity -> seems generous. Need to verify concurrency assumptions.

sasha: Important: us-west-2 has limited spare capacity in some AZs. For Dedicated we should avoid single-AZ pinning. Recommend spread across 3 AZs and reserve 10% headroom for AZ failover. Also check cross-AZ network egress — serving KV/cache traffic cross-AZ increases latency and cost.

infra-bot: cluster-metrics: us-west-2/dedicated-pool-alpha current utilization 62%, avg GPU latency p95 210ms, mem pressure 68%, io wait minimal. (metrics snapshot at 1779004500)

jon: Good catch on AZs. Proposal: size initial commit at 48 GPUs but configure request-routing policy to 40 GPUs steady + 8 burst (burst maps to reserved burst queue we backfill from spot/dedicated flexible capacity). That gives predictable committed baseline while letting us cover short spikes.

kevin: Agree. Also recommend quantization plan: push customers to q4_0 for chat model to drop per-GPU tokens/sec requirement by ~20%. That reduces required GPUs or improves tail latency. We'll need model QA and evals before switching.

maria: Finance flagged weird billing delta in last month's Dedicated billing report — committed discount applied but egress and ephemeral snapshots drove cost > expected. @finance-bot can you pull a cost breakdown for Alpha's last 30 days?

finance-bot: cost-summary: Alpha (us-west-2) last 30d: compute (committed) $134k, egress $24k, storage/snapshots $9.5k, networking cross-AZ $3.2k. Noted 18% higher than forecast due to snapshot frequency.

sasha: Snapshot frequency: they run hourly model snapshotting for fast rollbacks. We should offer compressed deltas or less-frequent snapshots on their Dedicated plan. That can cut storage+egress by ~60%.

kevin: Quick math for the commit sizing decision: if we guarantee 40 GPUs steady with 8 burst, and we take 10% AZ headroom, effective usable steady = 36 GPUs across AZs. With 36 GPUs * 30k tokens/s = 1.08M tokens/s steady. Given expected steady ~15k tokens/s we have huge cushion. So 48 commit is safe from throughput POV, but we should document worst-case assumptions and tail behavior.

jon: Action items: 1) infra: prepare a runbook for AZ spread + 10% failover policy. 2) eng-ml: run evals for q4_0 tradeoffs on customer's prompt set. 3) finance: produce a forecast with snapshot + egress optimizations applied. 4) product: draft canary rollout plan (start with 20% traffic on steady pool).

maria: I'll own coordination with the customer for canary windows and agree snapshot policy. For the rollout config we should include automatic fallback to hosted model variant if Dedicated pool saturates.

kevin: Also let's add a small monitoring alert: if commit pool utilization >75% for 10m, trigger auto-burst policy and notify oncall + customer.

sasha: Network note: enable local NVLink intra-node for heavy KV cache workloads and ensure the fleet is scheduled to avoid cross-AZ cache misses during canary.

jon: For the billing investigation, finance asked for the terraform plan we used to provision the pool. snippet they wanted:

```
module "dedicated_pool_alpha" {
  source = "./modules/dedicated-pool"
  region = "us-west-2"
  gpu_count = 48
  az_spread = 3
  snapshot_policy = "hourly"
}
```

maria: I'll update snapshot_policy to "daily-deltas" in the plan and re-run cost projection.

infra-bot: note: schedule window for deployment suggested 2026-04-02 02:00 UTC (low traffic).

maria: Thanks everyone — this is enough to brief sales + legal on the commit terms. I'll follow up with a summary doc and the canary playbook. :thumbsup:
